title: Causal Inference
tagline: Potential outcomes, randomised experiments, regression and matching, instrumental variables and LATE, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, synthetic control and external validity
summary: Did a policy work, and by how much? This course develops the modern toolkit for answering causal questions with data: the potential-outcomes framework, randomised experiments, regression and matching under selection on observables, instrumental variables and local average treatment effects, difference-in-differences and event studies, regression discontinuity and synthetic control. The emphasis throughout is on the assumptions each method needs and how to probe them.

chapters.title: Potential outcomes and causal effects
chapters.summary: Counterfactuals, average treatment effects, selection bias and causal diagrams.

chapters.title: Randomised experiments
chapters.summary: Why randomisation identifies causal effects, analysing experiments, statistical power, non-compliance and threats to validity.

chapters.title: Regression and matching
chapters.summary: Selection on observables, regression as weighted matching, propensity scores, and the limits of controlling for confounders.

chapters.title: Instrumental variables and local average treatment effects
chapters.summary: Natural experiments, the LATE theorem and compliers, and the problem of weak instruments.

chapters.title: Difference-in-differences
chapters.summary: Parallel trends, two-way fixed effects, event studies, and the pitfalls of staggered adoption.

chapters.title: Regression discontinuity
chapters.summary: Sharp and fuzzy designs, local estimation around a cut-off, bandwidth choice and tests for manipulation.

chapters.title: Synthetic control and comparative case studies
chapters.summary: Building a counterfactual from weighted comparison units, placebo inference and synthetic difference-in-differences.

chapters.title: External validity and the credibility revolution
chapters.summary: Generalising from experiments, heterogeneous effects, replication and pre-registration, and the use of evidence in policy.
